text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Czech rail workers' strike has paralysed rail transport between the Czech Republic and Slovakia. Before the strike, there were about 100 passenger and freight trains a day crossing the Czech-Slovak borders.
- Parliament has included a proposal of the opposition Party of Democratic Left (SDL) to postpone indefinitely banking prtivatisation on the agenda of its February session.
- The SDL said it was not sure that the junior governing coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), would support the banking sell-off postponement despite repeated pledges to do so.
- Other opposition parties said they were not against banking privatisation as such, but that they opposed the way the ruling coalition wants to carry out the move.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The paper quotes unnamed sources as saying another new member of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) governing board should be appointed next week. NBS Governor Vladimir Masar is expected to propose the head of the NBS banking supervision department Tibor Kasiak.

- The Bratislava Stock Exchange has added five new issues to the structure of its SAX index. The new shares are the steel wire producer Drotovna Hlohovec, drug maker Slovakofarma, chemical company Chemolak, construiction firm Vahosatv and alluminium maker ZSNP.

- Steel producer VSZ, one of the major Slovak exporters, said it expected to increase its exports in Europe by some 425,000 tonnes in 1997 against the previous year. Exports to CEFTA countries should increase by 327,000 tonnes, while sales on EU markets should rise by some 38,000 tonnes.
- VSZ said it would welcome faster removal of custom tarrifs among countries of the Central European Free Trade Agreement.

- Representatives of the Czech heavy engineering company Skoda Plzen a.s. and the Slovak engineering firm Povazske Strojarne held talks on possible cooperation in the field of production of gear boxes for Czech trucks Liaz and Tatra.
- VSZ invested about 3.5 billion crowns in modernisation programmes last year.

- SES Tlmace, an engineering company specialising in production of equipment for the energy sector, has won a contract worth five billion crowns for supplies of equipment for reconstruction of Vojany hydro power station.
